conversation.content:
Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that this can be a really challenging and overwhelming time for new mothers, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. 

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential areas of support that might be helpful to you during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it can help us get a sense of how you're coping with the transition to motherhood.

Please know that everything we discuss today is completely confidential, and I want to assure you that this is a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. I'm here to listen and to provide guidance and support, not to judge.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us understand your emotional well-being over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible.

So, let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself and your life in general over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually enjoy, or have you been feeling a bit down or overwhelmed?

.. to be honest, I've been feeling really tired and overwhelmed most of the time. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but it's just been really hard to enjoy the things I used to enjoy. Even simple things like taking a shower or reading a book feel like chores now. And when I do try to do something I used to like, it just doesn't feel the same. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? 

I've been worrying a lot about my baby's safety, too. Like, I'll be sitting there feeding her, and suddenly I'll think, "What if I'm not doing this right?" or "What if something happens to her?" And it's hard to shake those thoughts off. It's like my mind is always racing, even when I'm trying to relax. 

I do have some good moments, though. Like, when my baby smiles at me, it's like everything else just melts away, and I feel happy for a little while. But those moments are fleeting, and then I'm back to feeling anxious and overwhelmed again. I just feel like I'm not doing a good enough job as a mom, and that's really hard for me to deal with. I guess that's why I've been feeling a bit down and hopeless sometimes. It's just really hard to explain... *sigh*
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

.. I don't know if I've been able to laugh as much as I used to. I mean, sometimes my husband will try to make me laugh, and I'll smile, but it's not the same as really laughing, you know? It's like, I can see the humor in something, but it's just not as funny to me as it used to be. And even when I do laugh, it's not like it used to be. It's more like a polite laugh, just to be nice, rather than really feeling the joy or humor in something.

I think that's one of the hardest things for me, is that I just don't feel like myself anymore. I used to be a really happy, optimistic person, and now I just feel like I'm going through the motions. And even when my baby does something cute or funny, I'll smile, but it's not like I'm really feeling the joy that I should be feeling. It's like, I'm just so overwhelmed and anxious all the time, that it's hard for me to really enjoy anything, even the things that should be making me happy.

Sometimes I'll be playing with my baby, and she'll do something adorable, and I'll think to myself, "I should be laughing right now, I should be feeling happy," but it's just not there. And that makes me feel even more guilty, like I'm not being the mom I should be. It's just really hard, you know? *sigh*
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

.. to be honest, I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I used to love planning outings or trying new restaurants, but now it just feels like too much work. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or reading a book, just don't seem as appealing to me anymore.

I think it's because I'm just so exhausted all the time. Taking care of a new baby is overwhelming, and it feels like I'm just trying to survive from one day to the next. I don't really have the energy to think about things I'm looking forward to, because I'm just trying to get through the day.

And even when I do try to plan something, like a visit with friends or a trip to the park, I just end up worrying about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if the baby gets fussy? What if I forget something important? It's just hard for me to enjoy planning things or looking forward to them, because I'm always worried about something.

Sometimes my husband will suggest we do something, and I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but then I'll just start feeling anxious about it, and I'll end up not wanting to do it after all. It's like, I just don't have the emotional energy to enjoy things like I used to. And that's really sad for me, because I used to love trying new things and looking forward to fun activities. Now, it just all feels like too much. *sigh*
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot, actually. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is fussy, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If I'm tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough. If my husband is stressed, I think it's because I'm not supporting him enough.

I feel like I'm just constantly criticizing myself, and it's really hard to shake off that feeling. Even when my husband tries to reassure me that everything is okay, I just can't seem to let go of the guilt. I feel like I'm just not good enough, like I'm failing in some way.

And it's not just the big things, either. It's the little things, too. Like, if I forget to burp the baby, or if I don't get the laundry done on time. I'll just beat myself up over it, thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I do this?" It's like, I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, so I can pounce on myself and say, "See, I knew I wasn't good enough."

It's really exhausting, to be honest. I feel like I'm just walking around with this constant sense of self-doubt, always wondering what I'm doing wrong. And it's hard to enjoy the good moments, because I'm always worried about what's going to go wrong next. *sigh* It's just really hard to be kind to myself, I guess.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's me all the time, it feels like. I worry about everything. I worry about the baby's health, about her safety, about whether I'm doing everything right. I worry about my husband, about our relationship, about how we're going to manage financially. I worry about the future, about what's going to happen next week, next month, next year.

And it's not just big things, either. I worry about little things, too. Like, I'll be sitting there feeding the baby, and I'll start worrying about whether the formula is okay, or whether the baby is getting enough to eat. Or I'll be changing her diaper, and I'll start worrying about whether I'm doing it right, or whether I'm going to hurt her somehow.

It's like, my mind is just constantly racing, and I feel like I'm always on edge. I'll be sitting there, trying to relax, and suddenly I'll think of something that could go wrong, and I'll just start worrying about it. And it's hard to calm myself down, because my mind just keeps going back to all the things that could go wrong.

Sometimes I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could happen. Like, what if the baby gets sick? What if there's a fire in the house? What if something happens to my husband? It's like, my mind just starts spinning, and I feel like I'm trapped in this cycle of worry and fear.

And the worst part is, I know it's not rational. I know that most of the things I worry about are unlikely to happen. But that doesn't stop me from worrying. It's like, my brain just can't seem to shut off, and I'm stuck in this constant state of anxiety. *sigh* It's really hard to explain, but it's just like I'm always waiting for something to go wrong, and it's exhausting.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

.. yes. That's happened to me a few times, actually. I'll be sitting there, just doing something normal, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. It's like, my body just takes over, and I feel like I'm not in control anymore.

It's really scary, because I don't know what's triggering it. Sometimes it's when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start feeling overwhelmed. Other times, it's when I'm out in public, and I'll feel like everyone is staring at me. It's like, my mind just starts playing all these worst-case scenarios, and I feel like I'm going to lose control.

The worst part is, it's hard to calm myself down when it happens. I'll try to breathe deeply, or remind myself that everything is okay, but it's hard to shake off the feeling of panic. It's like, my body is just stuck in this state of high alert, and I don't know how to turn it off.

Sometimes, when it happens, I'll just start crying. It's like, my body is just releasing all this tension and anxiety, and I feel like I'm a mess. My husband will try to calm me down, but it's hard for him to understand what's going on. He'll be like, "What's wrong?" and I'll be like, "I don't know, I just feel scared." It's hard to explain, because it's not like there's a specific reason for it. It's just this feeling of panic and fear that comes out of nowhere.

It's really hard to deal with, because it makes me feel like I'm losing control. Like, I'm supposed to be this capable, competent mom, and yet I'm just falling apart. It's hard to admit, but it's true. I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and sometimes it feels like everything is just going to come crashing down. *sigh*
Things have been getting on top of me

.. yes. That's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to handle it. Taking care of the baby, managing the house, trying to be a good wife and friend... it's all just feeling really overwhelming.

Some days, I'll wake up and just feel like I'm drowning in responsibilities. I'll look around the house, and see all the laundry and dishes and mess, and just feel like I'm never going to get it all done. And then I'll think about the baby, and how I need to feed her and change her and soothe her, and it's just like... how am I going to do all of this?

I feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water, you know? Like, I'm just trying to survive from one day to the next, without too much of a disaster happening. But it's hard, because I feel like I'm not doing anything well. I'm not being a good enough mom, or wife, or friend... I'm just feeling like I'm failing all over the place.

And the worst part is, I don't know how to ask for help. I feel like I should be able to handle it all on my own, like I'm some kind of superhero or something. But the truth is, I'm just tired and overwhelmed and feeling really alone. I feel like I'm just trying to put on a brave face, but inside, I'm just barely holding it together.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, feeling like I'm just about to lose it, and my husband will come over and be like, "Hey, how are you doing?" And I'll be like, "I'm fine, I'm fine..." But really, I'm not fine. I'm just feeling really overwhelmed and scared, and I don't know how to admit it. *sigh* It's just really hard, you know?
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

.. yes. That's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and I think it's because I've just been feeling so unhappy and overwhelmed. I'll lie in bed at night, and my mind will just start racing with all these thoughts and worries. I'll think about the baby, and whether I'm doing everything right, and whether she's healthy and happy. I'll think about my husband, and whether we're okay, and whether we're going to make it through this tough time.

And then I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do, and all the things I'm not doing well enough. I'll think about the laundry, and the dishes, and the cleaning, and how I'm just not keeping up. I'll think about my body, and how it's not bouncing back from the pregnancy like I thought it would. I'll think about my relationships, and how they're all changing, and how I'm not sure who I am anymore.

It's just like, my mind is a constant whirlwind of worries and fears, and it's hard to shut it off. I'll try to relax, and take deep breaths, and remind myself that everything is okay, but it's just hard to calm down. And then, when I finally do fall asleep, I'll have these awful dreams, or I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and be wide awake for hours.

It's exhausting, you know? I feel like I'm just running on fumes all the time, and I don't know how to catch up. I'll try to take naps during the day, but even those are hard to come by, because the baby is always needing something. And when I do get a chance to rest, I just feel guilty, like I should be doing something more productive.

I guess what I'm trying to say is, I just feel really lost and alone right now. I feel like I'm just trying to survive, rather than really living. And it's hard, because I know I'm not alone, but it feels like it. It feels like everyone around me is just moving forward, and I'm just stuck in this rut, unable to get out. *sigh* Sorry, I'm just really struggling right now...
I have felt sad or miserable

.. yes. That's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I have this beautiful baby, and I love her so much, but sometimes it feels like that's not enough. Sometimes it feels like everything is just too much, and I'm just not happy.

I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying. I won't even know why I'm crying, I'll just be overwhelmed with this feeling of sadness. And it's not just when I'm alone, either. Sometimes I'll be with my husband, or with friends, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me.

It's hard, because I feel like I should be happy. I mean, I have this wonderful life, and this beautiful baby, and I should be grateful. But sometimes it just feels like everything is too much, and I'm just not coping. I'll feel like I'm failing as a mom, or as a wife, or as a person, and it's just really hard to shake that feeling.

Sometimes I'll try to talk to my husband about it, but it's hard to explain. He'll be like, "What's wrong?" and I'll be like, "I don't know, I just feel sad." And he'll try to reassure me, but it's hard to reassure someone who's just feeling really down.

I've even had thoughts of... not being here, anymore. Not in a serious way, I don't think, but just fleeting thoughts of, "What if I just didn't have to deal with all of this anymore?" And that's really scary, because I know that's not a healthy way to think. But it's just hard, you know? It's hard to feel like I'm drowning in all of this, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.

I guess what I'm trying to say is, I just feel really lost and alone right now. I feel like I'm just trying to survive, rather than really living. And it's hard, because I know I'm not alone, but it feels like it. *sigh* Sorry, I'm just really struggling right now...
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

.. yes. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll feel this lump in my throat, and the next thing I know, I'm just sobbing. It's not even always about anything specific, it's just... everything, I guess. The stress, the overwhelm, the feeling like I'm not doing anything right...

I've been crying in front of my husband, in front of my friends, even in front of the baby. It's like, I just can't help it. And it's not just a few tears, either. I mean, I've had full-on sobbing fits, where I'm just completely losing it. It's embarrassing, and it's scary, because I don't know how to stop it.

Sometimes I'll be in the middle of feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying. And I'll be like, "What's wrong with me? Why am I crying?" But it's just... everything is just so hard, and I feel so alone, even when I'm surrounded by people.

I've even cried in the shower, or in the car, when I'm alone. It's like, I just need to let it all out, you know? And sometimes it feels like the only way to do that is to just cry.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this strong, capable mom, and instead I'm just a mess. I feel like I'm failing everyone, including myself. And the crying just makes me feel even more like a failure, because I'm not supposed to be crying all the time. I'm supposed to be happy, and grateful, and all those things.

But the truth is, I'm just not. I'm sad, and I'm overwhelmed, and I'm struggling. And the crying is just a symptom of all that, I guess. *sigh* Sorry, I'm just really struggling right now...
